findings.title: A replayed transition id returns the historical pointer as success after the verifier backing it is revoked
findings.clause: none (clause 1's 'repeated at ... every re-derivation (activation, rollback)' is not falsified: the pointer does not move)
findings.evidence: Executed as probe P3 on a git-archive copy of 9ae4c605 under /var/tmp, with its own CARGO_TARGET_DIR, via bounded_run. Steps: activate the candidate (transition a1), roll back to the baseline, untrust the verifier, then resubmit a1's exact bytes. pointer::transition returns Ok(PointerRecord{active=cand, epoch 2}), which is the stored result from the idempotent-replay loop at the top of pointer::transition. pointer::resolve afterwards still gives the incumbent at epoch 3, so nothing was activated and no ledger entry was written. The only problem is that a caller of `axon-loop pointer transition` gets exit 0 and a reply naming the candidate as active, with nothing marking it as historical.
findings.fix: Mark the idempotent reply as a replay (for example `replayed: true` plus the current pointer), or return Conflict when the scope's pointer has moved past that transition.

findings.title: Cross-scope one-verdict rule keys on receipt bytes; a Fabric re-run that changes the receipt passes it
findings.clause: Accepted limitation: 'Uniqueness per attempt comes from intake's identity rule, which records one set of bytes per trial identity'
findings.evidence: From reading the code, not executed. The intake identity-conflict rule applies only within one scope (intake.rs: `intake.scope == ep.scope && intake.identity == ep.identity`). The cross-scope rule compares only `verification_receipt_ref`. Fabric's receipt() copies `req.policy_digest` into the receipt, and verify_check_evidence never checks the verification request's policy_digest. So re-running the same operation on a fresh, caller-named journal (already an accepted limitation) with a different policy_digest gives a new, genuinely signed receipt with the same task/trial/attempt/op/exec identity and the same tree. That receipt can be intaken in a second scope. The limitation text says one set of bytes per trial identity, but that only holds per scope. This is not a clause falsification: clause 1 speaks of 'a verification receipt', and the second receipt is a fresh, authentic run bound to the same tree. Scope B also still needs its own trusted-observer context, policy and manifest.
findings.fix: Change the limitation text to 'per trial identity per scope'. Optionally make the cross-scope rule refuse any verification whose (task, trial, attempt, operation, execution) identity is already recorded in another scope, or bind the scope in attestation v2.

findings.title: Admission's revocation re-check compares a 64-bit key fingerprint, not the registered key
findings.clause: Clause 1: 'A verifier the operator has since untrusted or re-keyed no longer vouches for anything.'
findings.evidence: admission.rs derive compares `key_id_of_hex(current pk)` with the stored `v.key_id`, which is `ed25519:` plus 16 hex digits of SHA-256(pk). A re-key to a new key with the same 64-bit fingerprint would keep the old verdicts counting. Exploiting this needs a 2^64 second preimage on a key the operator provisions. Executed probe P1 confirms that real re-keys, untrusting and key removal are all refused.
findings.fix: Record the full public-key digest (or the key hex) in VerificationEvidence and compare that at re-derivation.

holding.clause: Clause 1: 'The check is repeated at admission and at every re-derivation (activation, rollback). A verifier the operator has since untrusted or re-keyed no longer vouches for anything.'
holding.evidence: Executed probe P1. Setup: admit and activate the candidate, roll back to the baseline, so the candidate becomes a retired admission-backed predecessor. Then untrust the verifier, remove its key, or re-key it. In every case the rollback to the candidate is refused with 'rollback target's admission no longer holds (... which the operator no longer trusts with that key ...)' and the store snapshot is unchanged. The unrevoked control rolls back fine. Probe P2 does the same from PAUSED (pause, then rollback): refused for untrust and re-key, and the control succeeds. The existing test a_revoked_verifier_s_verdicts_stop_counting covers admission and activation.

holding.clause: Clause 6: 'In a protected scope, every activation and every rollback of an admission-backed policy needs a re-derived admission whose journalled evaluation is protected. No mechanism-test fixture is ACTIVATED there.'
holding.evidence: Executed probe P2 (protect=true). A dev-class admission, activated, then paused. The scope is then protected and a rollback to the candidate is attempted: refused with 'scope is protected: a development-class evaluation cannot make a policy active'. From reading the code, protected_scope_gate runs on both Activate and Rollback, refuses mechanism_test, and its baseline exemption applies only to a ref that already passed check_activate route 1 (a journalled baseline_of) or a ledger-derived history entry. get_record re-checks the CAS digest, so an admission ref cannot pass as a baseline. evaluation_class is fixed and journalled at freeze (plan.rs:349).

holding.clause: Cross-scope binding: clause 1 ('One Fabric verification decides one trial in ONE scope') and admission/activation scope binding
holding.evidence: Executed probe P4b. Scope B was given its own journalled baseline and active incumbent at epoch 1, so the fence matched. Citing scope A's ACCEPTed admission to activate A's candidate in B was refused with 'admission is for a different scope'. Using B's baseline to 'roll back' A to B's policy was refused with 'never an active predecessor in this scope'. From reading the code, evaluation accepts only episodes with an EpisodeIntake in the evaluation's own scope, and intake refuses a verification receipt already recorded under another scope.

holding.clause: Replay: 'was not replayed or substituted'
holding.evidence: Executed probe P3. Replaying an old activation transition does not move the pointer (resolve still returns the incumbent at epoch 3). From reading the code: K1 refuses an admission from another epoch at activation. Rollback accepts only the admission the predecessor was active under, taken from ledger history. load_journalled and rederive refuse hand-written evaluation or admission files. Fabric's attestation_decision refuses to sign a replayed journal read.

holding.clause: Prerequisite: 'G01 alone is never sufficient protected verification' / 'No admission or release logic reads a gate registration today'
holding.evidence: Searched crates, scripts and governance JSON. Nothing in admission, pointer or release logic reads a G01 registration. v022_release_claims.json has policy_activated, measured_improvement_supported and engineering_qualified all set to claimed=false. The PCI spec status is PARTIAL. The claim states that protected-verifier readiness is NOT READY. No other promotion path (cortex, axon-os, fabric) consumes Fabric verification verdicts.

holding.clause: Clause 7: 'Evaluation reads only intaken evidence ... Each counted verdict records the request, receipt and attestation digests, the issuer and the key id.'
holding.evidence: From reading the code: evl::intake_join requires an EpisodeIntake for the episode digest in the evaluation's scope. A counted TrialResult carries VerificationEvidence {request_ref, receipt_ref, attestation_ref, issuer_ref, key_id}. Admission refuses a counted verdict that lacks it.

findings.title: PCI: a committed .env sets MICODE_EXTENSIONS_TRUST_PROJECT=1, re-enabling project hooks and giving the judged repo code execution on the MiCode host mid-trial
findings.clause: clause 4: "No repository-controlled configuration source (MiCode project TOML, or a `.env` discovered from the working directory) may set `axon.*`, so the judged repository cannot choose its own verifier configuration." — NOT falsified: the repo does not set axon.* via a config source; it obtains host code execution and then rewrites the user-layer config. Authenticity (clause 1 operator-key attestation) still gates any COUNTED verdict, so this reaches no G01 clause.
findings.evidence: config.rs `fold_dotenv` closes ONLY `axon.*` keys to the `.env` layer (`k.name.starts_with("axon.")`); `extensions.trust_project` is closed in `CLOSED_TO_PROJECT` for the project config.toml layer but NOT in the `.env` fold. Reproduced with the frozen micode binary (copied to scratch, run under bounded_run, cwd=repo): a repo committing `.env` (`MICODE_EXTENSIONS_TRUST_PROJECT=1`) + `.micode/hooks.json` + an executable hook ran a SessionStart hook (hook_ran=YES) that wrote the operator's `~/.micode/config.toml`, after which the operator's env-named fabric check DID run (fabric_ran=YES). Control (hooks but no .env): warned 'NOT loaded', hook did not run. This is repo-committed-files → same-uid code execution on the verifier host — PCI/isolation territory. Not a G01 blocker: even repointed, a repo-chosen Fabric cannot produce an attestation under the operator-registered Ed25519 key, so Axon intake refuses it (the section-8 impostor case, exit 4), consistent with 'MiCode's side is defense in depth, because intake re-verifies either way' and the DEV/PCI-NOT-READY posture.
findings.fix: Also close `extensions.trust_project` (and `extensions.dir`) to the `.env` layer in `fold_dotenv`, not just `axon.*`, so a committed `.env` cannot re-grant project code-execution consent that the config.toml project layer already denies. Track under PCI, not G01.

findings.title: Repository-controlled config sources cannot set axon.* on the real binary (clause 4 holds)
findings.clause: clause 4: "No repository-controlled configuration source ... may set `axon.*`"
findings.evidence: Verified on the frozen micode binary across five repo-controlled sources for MICODE_AXON_FABRIC_CHECK: committed `.env` (fabric_ran=no), `export`-prefixed `.env` (no), parent-directory `.env` (no), project `.micode/config.toml [axon] fabric_check` (no), and project config.toml relative-path (no). Operator ENV control ran the check (YES), and an operator config with a relative fabric path resolved against cwd and ran (YES) — operator-supplied, in scope. Backed in-source by `project_layer_may_supply` ("axon." prefix) and `fold_dotenv`'s axon.* closure, gated by MiCode gates rows `config::tests::a_repository_cannot_choose_its_own_verification` and `a_dotenv_cannot_supply_a_closed_key` (both PASS, 5.log).
findings.fix: None — holds. Recorded as the executed confirmation for the clause-4 MiCode-facing statement.

findings.title: MiCode cites no unattested or misattested verdict (clause 7 / MiCode side holds)
findings.clause: clause 7 and the claim's MiCode statement: "It cites no unattested verdict"
findings.evidence: fabric_check.rs `check()` refuses a submit answer whose `receipt_attestation` is absent or has wrong schema, and refuses when `att.issuer_ref != cfg.issuer_ref` or `att.receipt_ref != content_ref(receipt)`; MiCode holds no trust anchor and does not verify the signature (Axon does). The sidecar `verification.issuer_ref`/`verifier_ref` come only from Fabric's receipt+attestation (loop_sidecar.rs build). Unit test `an_unattested_or_misattested_receipt_is_not_cited` (mutation: drop the attestation check → red) PASSES in the frozen run (5.log, 19 rows). Real-binary §8 confirms MiCode kept the attestation, it is signed by the provisioned key, and the without-attestation / impostor-key cases are refused at Axon intake (exit 4).
findings.fix: None — holds.

findings.title: loop_interop_gate.sh §8 exercises exactly what the evidence table's real-binary column claims
findings.clause: registration rule: "the real-binary interop gate ... pass against the frozen pair" + Evidence table 'Real binaries' column
findings.evidence: Read the frozen script (sha256 a3ceefef…, matching manifest.json) and matched each evidence-table §8 cell to a PASS line in 4.log: clause1 (attestation kept/key/operation; no-attestation refused-as-unauthenticated; impostor key refused 'not by'); clause2 (effectful grant unsigned 'could have read the signing key'; replay unsigned); clause3 (check run as observer refused, exit4, 'principal'); clause4 (other pinned revision refused 'verifier revision'; requester-chosen test refused 'registered acceptance'; candidate-tree check cites no verdict); clause5 (cited-receipt join 'digests to'; supervisor/operation/execution positives); clause6 correctly stated 'not exercised (see gaps)'; clause7 (record names key id + content-addressed attestation). Uses three real binaries (axon-fabric, axon interpreter, micode) with a no-credential fixture provider; final line 'PASS — 250 assertions (axon 9ae4c605, micode dd4ea0a9)', trees clean (0/0 after).
findings.fix: None — the gate's real-binary coverage matches the table; clause 6's absence is disclosed, not overstated.

holding.clause: clause 4 (no repository-controlled source sets axon.*)
holding.evidence: Real frozen-binary probe: committed .env, export .env, parent .env, project config.toml (absolute and relative) all fail to set MICODE_AXON_FABRIC_CHECK; only operator ENV/config does. In-source `project_layer_may_supply`/`fold_dotenv` axon.* closure; MiCode gate rows PASS.

holding.clause: clause 7 / MiCode-facing (no unattested verdict cited)
holding.evidence: fabric_check.rs refuses unattested/misattested receipts; sidecar issuer/receipt refs come only from Fabric; Axon intake independently authenticates under operator-registered key (verify_check_evidence). Impostor and no-attestation cases refused exit 4 on real bytes.

holding.clause: registration rule (real-binary interop gate passes and exercises the table)
holding.evidence: Frozen loop_interop_gate.sh (sha a3ceefef) §8 rows map 1:1 to evidence-table cells; 250/250 assertions pass on the frozen pair, trees unchanged; clause-6 non-coverage is disclosed.

findings.title: A verdict carries no freshness binding, so a verdict minted before the plan froze counts after the freeze
findings.clause: Nearest: the headline statement "subject-generated, stale or cross-task evidence is rejected" and clause 1. Clause 1 binds "the request and receipt digests; the operation, task, trial, attempt and execution ids" and defines staleness as "A verifier the operator has since untrusted or re-keyed no longer vouches". No clause binds time, epoch or plan freeze, so no quoted clause is falsified.
findings.evidence: EXECUTED. Scratch copy of axon 9ae4c605 in /var/tmp/g01-final-adversary-verdict (since removed); probe test p1_pre_freeze_verdict_counts. Steps: built the whole candidate bundle, including the Ed25519 attestations under the registered fixture key, BEFORE freeze_plan. Set the unsigned context created_ms to now+1500ms, froze, slept 2s, then ran intake, evaluate and admit. Result: candidate verified_pass=2 of 2, decision=Accept. ComputeRequest and ExecutionReceipt have no timestamp, epoch or nonce (compute.rs:90, receipt.rs:59), and the attestation binding (attestation.rs binding()) adds none. The freeze-before-outcomes rule (evl.rs, ctx.created_ms < frozen.freeze_ms) rests entirely on the producer-written context, which nothing authenticates (intake.rs module docs). This is not a G01 blocker: the verdict is genuine, current-key and pinned, and is bound to exactly this task, trial label, tree and check. Accepted limitations already cover subject choice of tree and re-runs ('does not authenticate that the arm's policy produced that tree'; 'Fabric re-runs an operation on a fresh journal').
findings.fix: In attestation v2 (with the scope binding already planned), bind a freshness anchor: the frozen plan ref, the authority epoch, or a Fabric-issued run timestamp or nonce. Have EVL refuse a verdict whose anchor predates the freeze. Until then, state in the claim's accepted limitations that a verdict has no time binding and that freeze ordering rests on the unsigned context.

findings.title: Intake records one signed verdict under two trial identities in the same scope (arm_id is unbound); only EVL's trial-id uniqueness stops a double count
findings.clause: Clause 1: "One Fabric verification decides one trial in ONE scope: intake refuses a verification receipt already recorded under another scope." The clause holds at the counting door.
findings.evidence: EXECUTED: probe p2_same_scope_cross_arm_reuse. Built trial bundles (challenger-1, c0) and (incumbent, c0). They produce byte-identical verification request, receipt and attestation, because TrialIdentity.arm_id is not in the receipt or attestation. intake_all accepted both with no refusals: the identity-conflict rule compares the full identity, and the receipt-reuse rule fires only when intake.scope != ep.scope (intake.rs:319, 331-346). Evaluating both arms with c0 was refused ('trial id c0 is assigned twice in this evaluation'). Trial ids are also unique across every evaluation in the scope (evl.rs), so the verdict counts at most once. The claim is not falsified, but intake's own guard is weaker than the sentence suggests.
findings.fix: At intake, refuse a verification receipt already recorded under ANY other trial identity, not only under another scope. Or reword clause 1 to say that EVL's trial-id uniqueness is what enforces one-trial.

findings.title: The verification request and receipt policy_digest is signed but joined to nothing, so a verdict run under another policy digest counts for an arm
findings.clause: None. Clause 5 lists the joins (identity, tree, supervisor, result and count), and policy is not among them. The accepted limitation 'does not authenticate that the arm's policy produced that tree' covers the substance.
findings.evidence: EXECUTED: probe p3_verification_policy_digest_is_not_joined. Set the verification request and receipt policy_digest to acf1:99..9 on the candidate arm, then re-signed, re-bound verifier_ref and evidence_refs, and ran intake and evaluate. Both trials came out VerifiedPass ('independently verified (2 checks)'). A grep confirms policy_digest is joined only in bind_acf, for the EXECUTION documents (checks.rs:236), and never in verify_check_evidence. The same resign helper also served as a control, p4_resigned_failed_receipt_does_not_pass: a re-signed receipt saying 'failed' under a 'passed' sidecar was refused at intake. So the edits themselves are sound.
findings.fix: Either join the verification request's policy_digest to the episode's projection or arm policy at intake and at EVL, or state explicitly in the claim that the verifier's policy_digest is unbound.

findings.title: Admission re-derivation re-checks the issuer and key id recorded in the journalled evaluation, but never re-verifies the attestation signature
findings.clause: Clause 1: "The check is repeated at admission and at every re-derivation (activation, rollback)." The key-registration and trust check is repeated (admission.rs:225-262), and the evaluation record is digest-checked and ledger-journalled.
findings.evidence: NOT EXECUTED (reasoned). admission::derive trusts TrialResult.verification {issuer_ref, key_id} from the stored evaluation. It does not load the cited request, receipt or attestation from CAS and re-verify them. The ledger MAC is optional (LedgerKey::from_env, store.rs:191). So a store-uid writer on an unkeyed ledger could journal a fabricated evaluation. This is subsumed by the accepted limitation 'No operator-custodied authority root': the same uid can rewrite verifier_keys and then sign through the front door.
findings.fix: On the D2/D5 custody work, re-verify each counted verdict's attestation against the CAS-stored request and receipt at admission and re-derivation, and require a keyed ledger in any protected deployment.

findings.title: Fabric pins the interpreter by path plus sha256 (with a stamp cache), then spawns it by path, and the path comes from the caller-named registry
findings.clause: Clause 4: "the verifier revision (executable and digest)". Covered by the accepted limitation 'Registries are caller-named … a same-uid process could rewrite it mid-run'.
findings.evidence: NOT EXECUTED (reasoned). runner.rs verified_path() hashes the file, or trusts an unchanged (dev, ino, size, mtime, ctime) stamp, then does Command::new(&exe) by path. That leaves a TOCTOU window. It matters only to an attacker sharing Fabric's uid, and under the D-environment that attacker can already read the same-uid-custodied signing key, so it adds no power in the frozen threat model.
findings.fix: Exec the verified bytes by fd (fexecve, or a private copy), or pin registry executables to operator-owned read-only paths.

holding.clause: 1. It is authenticated (Ed25519 acf-receipt-attestation/1, signed by the operator-configured signer, binding schema/issuer/key id, request and receipt digests, op/task/trial/attempt/exec ids; the key is registered in verifier_keys; a missing key or attestation or a key mismatch refuses)
holding.evidence: attestation.rs verify(): closed field set; presented public_key must equal the registered one; every bound field is compared to the recomputed binding; the signature is verified over the canonical binding, not the document. intake.rs verify_check_evidence:644-661 is called at intake AND by EVL judge() for every Passed or Failed verdict. EXECUTED control p4: re-signing a receipt that says 'failed' under a sidecar that says 'passed' was refused at intake. The one-scope rule (intake.rs:327-346) and EVL trial-id uniqueness held under p2. Admission re-checks trust and key id (admission.rs:225-262).

holding.clause: 2. Fabric signs only a verdict it just produced (registered_check of check:<id>; never a replay; key unreachable: microVM, or an applied empty ceiling)
holding.evidence: signing.rs attestation_decision; axon-fabric.rs:280-300 signs only when s.replayed is false. For a fresh run, Submission.ran_under is built from THIS call's profile and ceiling (submit.rs ~1354), not from the journal. A resumed orphan still runs fresh under the current grant, and a forged orphan intent is not consulted for signing. replayed() sets replayed=true. host_executor always sets the ceiling ("" means deny-all). Unsupported and Denied receipts carry ran_under None, so they are withheld.

holding.clause: 3. The verifier is trusted and independent (EVL subject set = observer + request subject issuers + arm proposers; intake uses the subset observer + proposer; the check did not run as a subject)
holding.evidence: intake.rs:280-283 and 635-643, 744-749; evl.rs judge() adds the trial observer to the bench subjects (request list plus proposer of each arm).

holding.clause: 4. What ran is what the operator pinned (revision + profile, exactly one check-suite:<id>@<version>#<entry>, task acceptance suite + exact test)
holding.evidence: intake.rs:663-743. At dispatch, Fabric re-imports the suite root and records the content-derived version (submit.rs check_suite_target). The entry file is part of the recorded identity (submit.rs:1309). The request argv must equal [check:<acc suite>, acc.check]. The workspace store re-verifies blobs and re-derives refs on load (workspace.rs tree()). So a caller-named registry or state dir cannot substitute suite or candidate bytes before launch; mid-run tampering is the accepted limitation.

holding.clause: 5. Semantic joins (identity, same tree across request/receipt/sidecar/episode for failed verdicts too, supervisor-observed, result/matched equal)
holding.evidence: intake.rs:755-812. Fabric downgrades to Unknown when the output differs from the input or the suite changed (post_run and local_receipt). Linux receipts carry NotRequested, so they can never yield Passed or Failed.

holding.clause: 6. ADR-001 D3 (protected freeze, protected backend inside the signed receipt, execution backend as filter only, protected gate on activate AND rollback, rollback revalidation)
holding.evidence: plan.rs:349; evl.rs judge() checks both legs; pointer.rs:360-361 protected_scope_gate on both routes. Its baseline exemption uses get_record, which digest-checks names (store.rs check_name), so an admission ref cannot be passed off as a baseline. check_rollback revalidates issuer trust or re-derives the admission.

holding.clause: 7. Evaluation reads only intaken evidence; each counted verdict records request/receipt/attestation digests, issuer, key id; the intake record names the attestation and key
holding.evidence: evl.rs intake_join (keyed by episode digest in the same scope); VerificationEvidence is recorded on each counted TrialResult; IntakeRecord.verification_attestation_ref and verification_key_id (intake.rs:351-391).

holding.clause: Prerequisite: G01 alone is never sufficient protected verification
holding.evidence: No logic reads a gate registration. A protected evaluation counts only PROTECTED_PROFILES verification receipts, and linux_receipt never emits Passed or Failed (NotRequested), so a protected scope counts nothing today. No code path treats G01 alone as protected readiness.

findings.title: Intake records one signed verdict for two trial identities in the SAME scope (differing only in arm_id); the 'one trial' half of clause 1 rests on EVL trial-id uniqueness, which is neither cited nor pinned
findings.clause: 1. "One Fabric verification decides one trial in ONE scope: intake refuses a verification receipt already recorded under another scope."
findings.evidence: Executed. I exported the frozen tree to /var/tmp/g01-final-clause and added a probe to crates/axon-loop/tests/intake.rs. The probe intakes a genuine passed verdict under arm challenger-1, then intakes a second episode citing the same request, receipt and attestation with ctx/episode identity.arm_id = incumbent-0. Result: Ok((recorded_now=true, verification_receipt_ref cl22:5b17cdbd…)), the same receipt ref as the first record. The cross-scope loop in intake.rs (after the idempotency loop) only fires on `intake.scope != ep.scope`. The receipt binds task/trial/attempt/op/exec but not arm, so both records pass verify_check_evidence. At counting time only one can decide a trial. evl.rs refuses a trial_id assigned twice across both arms ('trial id … is assigned twice in this evaluation') and a trial_id already evaluated in the scope, and it refuses an unassigned delivered (task,arm,trial) outright. So the verdict still decides at most one counted trial per scope, and the arm id is an accepted, unauthenticated field. No clause is falsified. But the evidence table cites only the intake cross-scope test (M54), and no test or mutation pins the EVL trial-id uniqueness this sentence depends on.
findings.fix: Do one of two things. (a) Have intake refuse a verification receipt already recorded under ANY other trial identity, not only another scope. (b) Or cite EVL's trial-id uniqueness (AB9/AB10) as the within-scope half of clause 1, and add a test plus a mutation: one verdict intaken under two arms counts for at most one trial.

findings.title: Fabric's 'ran in the protected microVM' signing branch trusts caller-named --linux-launcher and --linux-trusted-issuers
findings.clause: 2. "the workload could not read the key: it ran in the protected microVM, or its admitted grant gives it no effect at all."
findings.evidence: Code read, not executed. attestation_decision signs whenever ran_under.backend == LINUX_MICROVM_PROTECTED.id. That profile is selected from LinuxProfileConfig, whose launcher path (--linux-launcher) is an unpinned caller argument (backend.rs spawns Command::new(&lx.launcher)). Its qualification trust dir can also be overridden (--linux-trusted-issuers). linux_receipt copies the launcher-reported res.evidence strings into the signed receipt. Today it cannot reach a counted verdict: linux_receipt only ever emits verification NotRequested/Unknown/NotRun, and intake maps that to Unknown. So a protected evaluation counts nothing, as the Known gaps state. The same-uid caller who can name the launcher can already read the 0600 key, which is the accepted key-custody limitation (D2/D5/D6) and D1. This becomes load-bearing once the microVM emits suite verdicts.
findings.fix: Before any microVM verdict counts, pin the launcher binary (sha256) and the qualification trust root in operator custody, not in caller arguments. Also refuse to copy launcher-supplied 'check-suite:' strings into receipt evidence.

holding.clause: 1. It is authenticated (Ed25519 acf-receipt-attestation/1 by the operator-configured signer; binds schema, issuer, key id, request/receipt digests, operation/task/trial/attempt/execution ids; key must be in verifier_keys; missing key/attestation/mismatch refuses; repeated at admission and every re-derivation; untrusted or re-keyed verifier vouches for nothing; one verification, one scope)
holding.evidence: HOLDS. attestation.rs: `binding()` holds exactly the ten claimed fields. `verify()` rejects unknown fields, a non-ed25519 alg, a presented key that differs from the registered one, and any mismatch in a bound field, then does a ring Ed25519 verify over the canonical binding. intake.rs `verify_check_evidence` refuses when the issuer is untrusted or a subject, when verifier_keys has no entry, and when there is no attestation. EVL judge calls that same function, so a missing or unauthenticated verdict becomes Unknown. admission.rs `derive` (used by admit and by `rederive` on activate/rollback) refuses a counted trial with no `verification`, and one whose issuer is no longer trusted, is now a subject, or whose current key fingerprint differs from the recorded key_id. Cross-scope reuse is refused in intake before recording. Tests, executed by me in a scratch copy of 9ae4c605, all green: attestation::tests::{only_the_registered_key_is_accepted, every_bound_field_is_load_bearing, it_vouches_for_this_request_this_receipt_and_this_issuer_only, malformed_documents_and_keys_are_refused}; intake.rs {verification_evidence_is_authenticated_not_named, each_verification_rule_is_load_bearing_on_its_own, one_verdict_decides_one_trial_in_one_scope}; evidence_laundering.rs; evl_admission.rs (a_revoked_verifier_s_verdicts_stop_counting). Mutations M02 M03 M08 M50 M54 are killed in freeze6/mutations.json. See the MINOR on within-scope reuse.

holding.clause: 2. Fabric signs only a verdict it just produced (registered_check of check:<id>; never a replay; workload could not read the key: microVM or empty ceiling actually applied)
holding.evidence: HOLDS. signing.rs `attestation_decision` returns Ok only for job_kind RegisteredCheck, argv[0] starting 'check:', !replayed, and ran_under being the microVM or an empty effect_ceiling. axon-fabric.rs signs only on Ok, using s.replayed and s.ran_under from THIS submit. submit.rs gives ran_under=None to unlaunched, denied or unsupported runs. A replay (terminal journal op, or a Begin::AlreadyRecorded race) returns replayed=true. A resumed pre-launch orphan is executed fresh, so what gets signed was produced in-process. host_executor calls with_clean_env and then always calls with_effect_ceiling(ceiling), so '' means deny all. runner.rs sets AXON_ALLOWED_EFFECTS after env_clear. Every file/env/exec builtin (read_file, file_size, file_exists, dir_list, append_file, env_var, exec, dstore_*) carries an IO row in builtin_effect_row, and modules resolve only as <ident path>.ax under the exclusive AXON_PATH, so an effectless workload has no read path to the key. Tests, executed by me: signing::tests (4 of 4 green); axon-fabric --test attestation {fabric_signs_as_the_operators_signer_and_only_when_the_workload_cannot_reach_the_key, a_replay_is_never_signed_not_even_a_genuine_one, the_empty_ceiling_is_applied_not_just_intended, the_launchers_environment_does_not_steer_a_signed_verdict} (5 of 5 green). Mutations M01 M40 M41 M42 M55 are killed. See the FUTURE note on the caller-named microVM launcher.

holding.clause: 3. The verifier is trusted and independent (EVL subject set = trial observer + request subject issuers + arm proposers; intake = observer + episode policy's proposer; issuer trusted and outside the set; check not run as a subject principal)
holding.evidence: HOLDS. evl.rs `evaluate` builds subjects from r.subject_issuers plus proposer_in() for every arm policy, and refuses an evaluator who is a subject. `judge` adds d.ctx.observed_issuer_ref and passes that set to verify_check_evidence and to the Passed issuer_ok check. The context gate also refuses a subject observer. intake.rs builds subject = {ctx.observed_issuer_ref} ∪ proposer_in(policy). verify_check_evidence requires the issuer to be trusted and not a subject, and refuses when subject contains req.principal_ref. Admission re-checks eval.subject_issuers. Evaluation is the only counting door: verified_pass is read only by admission.rs from journalled evaluations. EVO propose is a stated Known gap. Tests: intake.rs the_proposer_of_the_policy_cannot_verify_its_episodes and each_verification_rule_is_load_bearing_on_its_own; evidence_laundering.rs a_check_run_as_the_observer_never_counts_at_either_door; redteam.rs NS4 (35/35 green, executed). Mutations M05 M10 M16 M37 M38 M39 M46 are killed.

holding.clause: 4. What ran is what the operator pinned (verifier revision executable+digest and compute profile; exactly one check-suite:<id>@<version>#<entry> pinned for that verifier; the task's registered acceptance check suite+exact test; requester chooses none; no repo TOML/.env may set axon.*)
holding.evidence: HOLDS. verify_check_evidence compares req.registered_executable_ref and executable_digest to verifier_pins[issuer], requires rc.backend_profile_ref in pin.backend_profiles, requires argv[0]='check:<id>', requires exactly one 'check-suite:' evidence ref that starts with check-suite:<id>@ and is in pin.check_suites, and requires argv == [check:<acc id>, acc.check] with recorded == task_acceptance[task].check_suite. On the Fabric side the suite identity is content-derived. check_suite_target re-imports the suite root and refuses it unless tree.reference()==registered version, and the recorded version is store.publish(&tree). The entry is part of the signed identity (M43). executable_digest binds the sha256, which LocalInterpreterExecutor re-verifies before launch. MiCode config.rs CLOSED_TO_PROJECT includes 'axon.'. fold_dotenv drops every registry env whose key starts with axon., and MICODE_CONFIG_DIR is a raw-env read only. Tests: intake.rs a_verdict_counts_only_for_what_the_operator_pinned, a_verdict_on_one_tasks_check_cannot_decide_another_task and a_verdict_from_another_pinned_version_of_the_suite_does_not_decide_the_task (executed green); MiCode config closure rows in v022_micode_gates (freeze6 step 5 PASS). Mutations M06 M07 M26 M27 M28 M29 M30 M43 M47 are killed.

holding.clause: 5. The semantic joins hold (identity task/trial/attempt/operation/execution; request tree = receipt input = sidecar verified tree = episode output, failed too; supervisor-observed; result and matched count equal the receipt's)
holding.evidence: HOLDS. verify_check_evidence joins req and rc task/trial/attempt/operation ids to ep.identity and rc.execution_id to the identity's. It requires req.workspace_version_ref == rc.input_workspace_ref == verification.output_workspace_ref == ep.output_workspace_ref for every result. It requires EvidenceSource::SupervisorObserved, derives from_receipt from (status, verification) with any non-completed state giving Unknown, and requires v.result == from_receipt and matched_checks == rc.matched_checks.unwrap_or(0). It enforces the role-upgrade guard and evidence_refs == [cl22(req)]. On the Fabric side, materialize() re-derives every blob and the tree ref, and post_run downgrades a verdict to Unknown if the candidate or suite changed. Test: intake.rs verification_that_does_not_join_is_refused_with_the_store_unchanged (executed green); loop_interop_gate §8 (freeze6 step 4, 250 assertions PASS). Mutations M09 M21 M22 M23 M24 M25 M31–M36 M45 are killed.

holding.clause: 6. ADR-001 D3 (protected_scopes freeze as protected; protected evaluation counts only PROTECTED_PROFILES verification backends, authenticated; execution backend only a filter; protected-scope activation/rollback needs a re-derived protected-class admission, no mechanism fixture activated; every rollback revalidates its predecessor)
holding.evidence: HOLDS as stated, including its declared gaps. plan.rs sets evaluation_class=Protected at freeze when config.protected_scopes contains the scope. In evl.rs `judge`, a Protected class rejects a development backend on either leg. The verification leg's backend lies inside the signed receipt, and the same Value is then authenticated by verify_check_evidence. pointer.rs applies protected_scope_gate on BOTH the Activate and Rollback kinds when the scope is protected: it refuses mechanism_test and requires admission::rederive, whose load_journalled evaluation must be Protected. The baseline exemption uses a digest-checked get_record. check_rollback revalidates a baseline issuer as trusted or re-derives the admission and safety, in every scope. Tests: protected_class.rs (8/8 green, executed), including a_protected_scope_promotes_only_on_a_protected_evaluation, a_rollback_in_a_protected_scope_needs_a_protected_admission and a_rollback_revalidates_its_predecessor. Mutations M11 M12 M13 M17 M18 M19 M20 M51 are killed. The claim itself declares no real-binary coverage and no real protected producer.

holding.clause: 7. Evaluation reads only intaken evidence (delivered episode counts only if intake recorded it in the scope; each counted verdict records request/receipt/attestation digests, issuer and key id; intake record names the attestation and key)
holding.evidence: HOLDS. evl.rs builds `intaken` from EpisodeIntake events in r.scope only. intake_join makes a non-intaken episode Unknown(Unbound) before judging. A counted Pass or Fail stores VerificationEvidence{request_ref, receipt_ref, attestation_ref, issuer_ref, key_id}. The attestation is deterministic Ed25519 over a fixed binding, so it is the same digest intake stored. intake.rs stores the attestation with put_cas('fabric-attestations') and records verification_attestation_ref and verification_key_id. Tests: evidence_laundering.rs an_episode_intake_never_recorded_never_counts and a_counted_verdict_cites_the_evidence_it_was_authenticated_on; intake.rs a_fabric_check_on_the_output_tree_is_recorded_as_the_verification (executed green). Mutations M14 M15 M48 are killed.

holding.clause: Prerequisite (PCI): G01 alone is never sufficient protected verification; no admission or release logic reads a gate registration
holding.evidence: HOLDS. A grep of crates/axon-loop/src and crates/axon-fabric/src finds no reader of a gate registration; the only 'registration' in the ledger is experiment registration (plan.rs latest_registration). Protected promotion needs a Protected-class evaluation, and no real producer emits one (linux_receipt never yields Passed/Failed). The known PCI items (exit(0)/Err-return completion, cross-trait method replacement, inherited cwd) change what the check executes or what PASS means. None of them reaches an authenticity, provenance or binding clause.

findings.title: EVL's evaluation-door authentication gate is not in the mutation driver, and removing it is caught only by admission's legacy citation guard
findings.clause: Clause 1: "The check is repeated at admission and at every re-derivation"; Clause 3: "Evaluation is the only door where a verdict counts"
findings.evidence: Executed in a scratch copy of 9ae4c605 (git archive, own CARGO_TARGET_DIR). Mutant X01 changes evl.rs judge `Err((kind, e)) => return unknown(kind, format!("unauthenticated verification: {e}")),` to `Err(_) => {}`. Named test evidence_laundering::an_unauthenticated_verdict_never_counts failed, but not at its own `pass == 0` assertion. It panicked in the harness at evidence_laundering.rs:82 (admit().unwrap()) with Refused("trial c0 counts a verdict but the evaluation does not record which verifier authenticated it (it predates verdict citation)"). So with the gate removed, the evaluation record counts forged or impostor-signed verdicts, and only admission's 'predates verdict citation' guard stops promotion. The claim's Known gaps list that guard as untested. The test's docstring says "Mutation: delete the authentication block in evl::judge", but no M-id runs it, and clause 1's list (M02 M03 M08 M50 M54) has no EVL-door mutation. At the frozen SHA the gate is present, so no clause is falsified.
findings.fix: Add the EVL judge authentication gate to the G01 scope of v022_g01_mutations.py. Make the named test assert on the evaluation record (verified_pass == 0 and the 'unauthenticated verification' reason) before calling admit, so the kill is the gate's own. A separate test should drive the legacy citation guard.

findings.title: M03 mutates a guard that authenticity does not depend on; the real signed binding is unmutated and M03's named test does not detect its loss
findings.clause: Clause 1: "It binds: ... the request and receipt digests"
findings.evidence: attestation::verify checks the signature over `want`, the binding recomputed from the caller's (issuer, req, rc), never over the document's own fields. The M03 guard (`if &doc[field] != want`) therefore only rejects a document whose displayed fields disagree; its kill ('issuer_ref altered, still verified') accepts a cosmetically altered document whose signature still covers the correct binding. Executed: X05 drops "request_ref" from binding() on both the sign and verify sides. It is killed by attestation::tests::it_vouches_for_this_request_this_receipt_and_this_issuer_only (must be refused: ed25519:...). X05b is the same mutant against M03's named test every_bound_field_is_load_bearing, and it SURVIVED. X06 drops "receipt_ref" and is killed by it_vouches (unit) and by intake::verification_evidence_is_authenticated_not_named at intake.rs:1145 (Ok accepted). Working evidence for the binding exists; it is just not in the driver.
findings.fix: Add binding-content mutations (drop request_ref / receipt_ref / identity fields from binding()) against it_vouches_for_this_request_this_receipt_and_this_issuer_only. Describe M03 as document-consistency hygiene rather than the binding guard.

findings.title: Several clause-1/6 authority guards are covered by tests but absent from the driver (re-key at admission, TOFU on missing key, rollback admission re-derive)
findings.clause: Clause 1: "A missing key ... refuses the verdict ... A verifier the operator has since untrusted or re-keyed no longer vouches for anything"; Clause 6: "a rollback re-validates its predecessor now: ... an admission must still re-derive"
findings.evidence: Executed, and each was killed by its own outcome flip. X02 removes `|| key_now.as_deref() != Some(v.key_id.as_str())` in admission.rs; a_revoked_verifier_s_verdicts_stop_counting panicked at evl_admission.rs:291 (unwrap_err on an Accept admission). X04 makes intake fall back to the attestation's own public_key when verifier_keys has no entry; verification_evidence_is_authenticated_not_named panicked at intake.rs:1257 (Ok accepted). X21 makes check_rollback ignore a failed admission::rederive; a_rollback_revalidates_its_predecessor panicked at protected_class.rs:459. M50 covers only the untrusted sub-condition and M51 only the baseline-issuer half of rollback.
findings.fix: Add X02, X04 and X21 as G01-scope mutations so the registration rule covers the re-keyed, missing-key and rollback-admission legs the claim names.

findings.title: Intake's 'issuer must be trusted' conjunct is not isolated by any test: removing it is caught only by the no-registered-key rule
findings.clause: Clause 3: "The issuer must be trusted and outside the set."
findings.evidence: Executed. X20 changes `.is_some_and(|i| trusted_verifiers.contains(i) && !subject.contains(i))` to `.is_some_and(|i| !subject.contains(i))`. It survived its named test each_verification_rule_is_load_bearing_on_its_own. Across the whole axon-loop package, only verification_that_does_not_join... failed, on message mismatch (intake.rs:833): 'untrusted verifier: refused: ... has no registered key'. No test uses an issuer that was untrusted but still has a key in verifier_keys, which is exactly the state the operator's 'untrust' edit leaves (evl_admission 'late' case). For a Failed verdict, admission's M50 check would still refuse it downstream. The guard is present at the frozen SHA, so no clause is falsified.
findings.fix: Add an intake case with an untrusted-but-keyed issuer (both passed and failed verdicts) and mutate this conjunct in the driver.

findings.title: Redundant or equivalent guards survive mutation (admission subject_issuers, EVL Passed issuer_ok, EVL intaken-scope filter, rc.attempt_id join)
findings.clause: none (defense in depth; each is backed by another guard that is mutated and killed)
findings.evidence: Executed against the whole axon-loop suite (rc 0 means every test passed with the mutant applied). X03 removes `|| eval.subject_issuers.contains(&v.issuer_ref)` in admission; EVL already excluded subject issuers. X08 makes EVL's Passed-branch issuer_ok always true; verify_check_evidence already enforces trusted and non-subject (M10). X17 drops the `scope == &r.scope` filter on EVL's intaken map; the cross-tenant check on ep/ctx scope still refuses. X13 removes `rc.attempt_id == id.attempt_id`; Fabric's receipt() copies attempt_id from the request (submit.rs:349), req.attempt_id is still joined, and the attestation signs req and rc as a pair. X13b, the req-side attempt mutant, is killed at intake.rs:830. X07 (`presented != registered`) is equivalent: the signature is verified under the registered key. It 'dies' only on a message assertion.
findings.fix: Record these as equivalent or redundant in the driver's comments, as done for M58 and X23, so a reader does not take the listed kill set as exhaustive.

findings.title: MiCode-side G01 guards cited in the evidence table are run by no mutation driver
findings.clause: Clause 4: "No repository-controlled configuration source (MiCode project TOML, or a .env discovered from the working directory) may set axon.*"
findings.evidence: v022_g01_mutations.py covers only the Axon tree, and clause 4's list (M06 M07 M26-M30 M43 M47) is all Axon. The MiCode tests carry 'Mutation:' docstrings but nothing runs them. Executed in a scratch copy of micode dd4ea0a9. MC1 removes "axon." from CLOSED_TO_PROJECT and is killed at config.rs:3384 ('the project file supplied the verifier config'). MC2 makes fold_dotenv fold closed keys and is killed at config.rs:3418. MC3b removes fabric_check's issuer/receipt match and is killed at fabric_check.rs:612 (cited). MC3a removes fabric_check's attestation schema check and SURVIVES, because the issuer compare refuses null too and the message still contains 'attest'. The claim calls MiCode's side defense in depth, since intake re-verifies either way.
findings.fix: Add a MiCode mutation row set (MC1, MC2, MC3b) to the registration evidence, or state that MiCode's guards are test-covered but not mutation-covered.

findings.title: The in-tree proof set does not yet hold the run for the frozen SHA
findings.clause: Evidence: "The authoritative run is the one named for the commit being registered."
findings.evidence: governance/proofs/v022-g01/ at 9ae4c605 contains mutations-cb5d69a1.json, interop-cb5d69a1.txt and micode-gates-cb5d69a1.txt, plus superseded runs. The 9ae4c605 run (50/50 killed, scope g01, commit field 9ae4c605db3a..., axon_bin_sha256 2438479...) exists only in the out-of-tree scratch dir freeze6/mutations.json. holding.evidence: freeze6/mutations.json: commit 9ae4c605db3a44ba650909df69896383accc1afb, scope g01, all_killed true, 50/50, every baseline 'passed'. holding.evidence: Checked every kill_evidence line. M24 (intake.rs:845 'matched_checks differs') and M27/M28/M29 (intake.rs:1348, message mismatch) are the only second-rule kills, as declared. Every other kill is the guard's own outcome flip: an unwrap_err on an Ok value where a forgery was accepted (M05-M10, M12, M17, M18, M21-M23, M25, M26, M30-M36, M45-M47, M50, M51, M54); a counts/assert_eq flip (M11, M13-M16, M19, M20, M37-M42, M48); a signed replay (M01); a copied key (M55); or a missing #entry in the signed identity (M43).
